**8B.4 Research Note: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2024**

Overall reading: **partial yes, with strong caveats**. Sisi did place capable technocrats into parts of the economic and social-policy apparatus, and some macro and welfare programs show real implementation capacity. But the core security and information apparatus remained heavily personalist, loyalist, and coercive, which limits the case that he broadly selected and empowered independent professionals.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| President El-Sisi Meets Prime Minister and Members of the New Government | State Information Service | 2024-07-03 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/ | Sisi told the new government to strengthen institutional frameworks, improve inter-agency coordination, and emphasize integrity and transparency. This is direct evidence that he wanted the bureaucracy staffed and used to execute a defined program. | 8B.4, 8B.3 |
| President Sisi swears in new government ministers | State Information Service | 2024-07-03 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-sisi-swears-in-new-government-ministers/ | The July reshuffle brought in broad technocratic portfolios covering economic management, energy, science, foreign affairs, and social policy. That supports a reading that Sisi did empower capable administrators in at least part of the state. | 8B.4 |
| PR 24/208: Egypt IMF reaches agreement on the 3rd review of the EFF | IMF | 2024-06-06 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/06/pr-24208-egypt-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-3rd-review-of-the-eff | The IMF described a reform agenda centered on private-sector-led growth, fiscal space for health and education, and reducing the state’s role. That is strong evidence that technocratic economic officials were shaping and executing policy, not just serving as figureheads. | 8B.4 |
| PR 24/59: Egypt staff and authorities reach agreement on reviews under the EFF | IMF | 2024-03-06 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement | The authorities agreed to flexible exchange rates, tighter macro policy, more social spending for vulnerable groups, and less preferential treatment for state-owned enterprises. This is concrete evidence of a technocratic policy team being empowered to implement adjustment. | 8B.4 |
| Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs | World Bank | 2024-05-28 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs | Takaful and Karama is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and run through proxy means testing, a grievance mechanism, and a dynamic social registry. That points to capable administrative execution in social policy. | 8B.4 |
| Egypt's Sisi names new armed forces chief of staff, defence minister | Reuters | 2024-07-03 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypts-sisi-names-ex-defence-140545714.html | Sisi replaced the defense minister and chief of staff, but then moved the outgoing officials into presidential adviser roles. This shows he could manage the security hierarchy, but the pattern is insider recycling, not open empowerment of independent professionals. | 8B.4, 8B.3 |
| Egypt's Sisi replaces head of powerful general intelligence agency | Reuters | 2024-10-16 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Egypt-s-Sisi-replaces-head-of-powerful-general-intelligence-agency-48090165/ | The intelligence chief was replaced by his deputy and the outgoing chief remained close as an adviser. That suggests continuity inside a politically embedded security network, not a clean meritocratic break. | 8B.4, 8B.3 |
| Egypt’s Al-Sisi Has Caged Himself In | Human Rights Watch | 2024-02-26 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/26/egypts-al-sisi-has-caged-himself | HRW argues Sisi relies on coercion and the military/security services rather than a normal party structure, and that independent institutions were hollowed out. This is strong negative evidence against broad empowerment of autonomous capable professionals. | 8B.4 |
| Egypt: New Laws Entrench Military Power Over Civilians | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-05 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/05/egypt-new-laws-entrench-military-power-over-civilians | HRW says new laws expanded military authority over civilians and gave the state more tools to pressure businesses. That supports the view that Sisi empowered coercive administrators and the military network more than neutral professionals. | 8B.4, 8B.3 |
| Egypt: Spate of Free-Speech Prosecutions | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-29 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions | HRW reported prosecutions of critics and journalists, including a case tied to reporting on a corruption investigation involving senior pro-Sisi party members. This suggests the state still protected the ruling network rather than empowering independent scrutiny. | 8B.4 |
| Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/ | Amnesty documented arrests of protesters, workers, and online critics over economic discontent. This shows the regime still empowered coercive security actors when criticism became politically costly, which cuts against a clean technocratic reading. | 8B.4, 8B.3 |

**Search gap**

- I found **good evidence for technocratic empowerment in economic and welfare policy**, but **limited direct evidence** on whether Sisi systematically selected and empowered capable people across the full state.
- The strongest negative evidence is in the **security and information apparatus**, where loyalist recycling, repression, and media control remain dominant.
- I did **not** find strong, independent evidence that Sisi built a broad meritocratic кадровый system or that capable professionals gained durable autonomy from the presidency.

**Best synthesis for 8B.4**

- Sisi **did** empower capable people in some policy areas, especially economic stabilization and targeted social programs.
- He **did not** broadly empower independent professionals across the state.
- The overall pattern is **selective competence under personalist control**: technocrats where needed, loyalists and coercive administrators where power needed protection.
